From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, jordan.ellis@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 14:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s — production traffic rejection (remediation update)

Team / Jordan — investigation complete and remediation deployed. Summary below: 

Root cause (summary):
- A policy-rollout job executed 2027-01-09 02:12 UTC introduced a malformed override for tenant acme-health-prod. Instead of applying a per-client rate limit, the rollout created a per-tenant cap with a low default (conservative burst) which became effective during the morning traffic peak. The policy engine accepted the patch without validation due to a gap in the rollout schema check.

Actions taken (11:20–14:15 PST):
1) Rolled back the 2027-01-09 policy patch for acme-health-prod.
2) Manually adjusted tenant burst and steady-state limits to the pre-rollback values.
3) Added a temporary +30% burst allowance for the next 24 hours while we stabilize (will auto-expire).
4) Ran end-to-end synthetics from three edge regions to validate no 429s observed after change.
5) Created a config diff (config_diff.patch) showing the patch vs. rollback and uploaded the remediation runbook (remediation-runbook.pdf).

Current status: normal — monitoring shows error-rate back down to baseline (0.3%). No dropped messages in the last 45 minutes. We will keep rate-limiter metrics on a 1-minute cadence and post a follow-up TOMR (technical owner monitoring report) at EOD.

Longer-term follow-ups (tracked):
- Add rollout schema validation to reject per-tenant caps unless explicitly approved (P0).
- Postmortem doc and RCA captured here: https://redwood.app/internal/postmortem/RC-20270110-429
- Plan to add automated smoke tests for tenant-specific policy rollouts (P1).

Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Hi Jordan and Bill — following up now that we've completed the initial postmortem and stabilization work. Thanks again for flagging this and for your patience while we worked through remediation. TL;DR below, with next steps and the compensations we've applied.

TL;DR
- Impact: ~20 minutes of elevated 429s during morning peak (08:55–09:15 PST) caused retries and delayed ingestion for some pipelines.
- Root cause: policy-rollout introduced an unintended per-tenant cap (see Dev's note).
- Remediation: rollback + temporary burst increase; monitoring confirms return to baseline.

Customer-facing items we've completed:
- Applied a 24-hour +30% burst buffer immediately during remediation.
- Applied a one-time service credit: 200,000 generation tokens and 50,000 embedding tokens to Acme Health account (ref: ACME-ENT-2026-09).
- Shared remediation artifacts: config_diff.patch, remediation-runbook.pdf.
- Postmortem link: https://redwood.app/internal/postmortem/RC-20270110-429

Planned engineering changes (tracking):
- P0: Block rollout of per-tenant caps without multi-signer approval and add schema validation.
- P1: Automated smoke tests for policy rollouts and expanded canary window.
- P2: Dashboard alert that correlates tenant config rollouts with elevated 429s.

If you'd like a walkthrough of the postmortem or want our engineering team to join a 30-minute review with your ops team, we're happy to schedule — suggest Wed 2027-01-13 09:00–10:00 PST or Thu 2027-01-14 11:00–12:00 PST.

Thanks again — please let me know if you see any further anomalies.

Warmly,
